newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends ends lower on local liquidation.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends ends lower on local liquidation.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled weaker on local liquidation on the close and earlier fund selling, floor sources said.
The benchmark December contract finished 0.50 lower to 74.45, having ranged from 75.70 to 74.35. October ended 0.51 weaker at 73.79, while the back months closed 0.35 lower to 0.10 higher.
Market sources have anticipated lower prices in the face of a healthy U.S. crop and strong foreign production.

Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A&M University, is one of several industry sources forecasting a higher production figure in the U.S. Department of Agriculture's October report.
He put U.S. output at 18.8 million bales in 1996/97. The USDA pegged the crop at 18.577 million bales August 12.
"There is no reason for this market to turn bullish other than technicals," Anderson said.
